name: Pterostilbene
short: Trial, 80 adults, high cholesterol: pterostilbene alone raised LDL (not with grape extract); high dose cut blood pressure. Safety analysis: no significant adverse reactions; none in 30 healthy men.
text: In a 6- to 8-week randomised, placebo-controlled trial in 80 adults with high cholesterol, pterostilbene taken alone increased LDL cholesterol (by 17.1 mg/dL), an effect not seen when it was combined with grape extract; the higher dose also lowered systolic and diastolic blood pressure, and the authors reported that taking a cholesterol medicine at baseline appeared to lessen the LDL effect. A safety analysis of a trial with the same design (80 adults with high cholesterol in the same four groups for 6 to 8 weeks; neither abstract says whether it is the same trial) found no adverse drug reactions on liver, kidney or glucose markers and no statistically significant self-reported or major adverse reactions. In a 12-week placebo-controlled pilot trial in 30 healthy men, no adverse events were reported. The cited trials lasted 12 weeks at most. Apart from the observation about cholesterol medicines, no interaction data were found in the cited sources.
